summary: Connection backlog amplification from partner webhook burst leading to runtime GPU-driver resets and persistent 5xx floor
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-12 19:02 UTC we observed an elevated 5xx error-rate from API Gateway for a subset of VectorSync traffic. Investigation shows an abnormal burst of inbound webhooks from a third-party partner integration that saturated the API Gateway accept queue and amplified connection backlog toward the serving runtime. Upstream runtimes started reporting NVML/gpu-driver resets and watchdog restarts, causing a persistent 5xx floor for ~18 minutes. Impact: VectorSync saw degraded successful request rate and increased tail latency; several customer requests timed out or returned 502/503. Scope: Multi-tenant production cluster (prod:us-west) with spillover into us-east via routing failover.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate a partner webhook fanout: 4500 concurrent HTTP/2 POSTs to /v1/generate for tenant VectorSync over 60s with keepalive enabled
2) Ensure payloads include ~20k token prompts to increase runtime GPU memory and KV cache activity
3) Observe API Gateway accept-queue depth growth and connection backlog; watch serving-runtime logs for NVML reset events
4) Verify resulting 5xx elevation on API Gateway metrics and degraded success rate for affected tenant
logs: 2026-03-12T19:04:11Z apigw[edge-1] ACCEPT_QUEUE=98 backlog=72 tenant=vector-sync route=/v1/generate status=throttled
2026-03-12T19:04:28Z runtime[node-a] ERROR NVML: GPU driver reset detected (pid=10233) - watchdog triggered; preempt_count=3
2026-03-12T19:07:45Z scheduler[autoscaler] INFO scale_decision=hold - prefetched shards in flux; avoid immediate scaling to reduce churn
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: autoscaler or prefetch hotloop causing increased CPU/GPU contention. Rejected after correlating NVML resets directly with connection backlog spikes.
Confirmed inbound webhook spike originated from partner domain webhook.partner-sync.com — VectorSync acknowledged a misconfigured retry storm on their side.

API Gateway accept queue filled quickly due to many long-lived connections (keepalive, HTTP/2) and large request bodies; this amplified proxy->runtime backlog and increased KV cache pressure on GPU memory.
Runtime telemetry shows repeated GPU driver resets (NVML) on nodes serving the tenant; kernel logs show repeated NVML timeouts and watchdog restarts between 19:03 and 19:21 UTC.
Prefetch and batching metrics: batching increased average sequence length leading to larger kernel allocations; combined with backlog it pushed some runtimes into OOM-and-reset cycles.
Routing behavior: when us-west nodes degraded, traffic shuffled to us-east causing partial cross-region amplification but failover worked as designed.
Relevant dashboards: apigw.accept_queue, runtime.nvml_resets, serving.kv_evictions, autoscaler.action_history.
customer_impact: VectorSync reported increased failed requests (502/503) for background sync jobs and elevated latency for user-facing generation calls. Estimated affected request volume: ~12k requests over the 18-minute window; revenue-impacting: yes (enterprise SLA-tier).
mitigation_taken: Applied emergency ingress rate-limit for tenant VectorSync at edge (rate limit: 1500 rps sustained, burst 500) at 19:08 UTC which reduced accept queue growth
Temporary disable of long-lived connection reuse for that tenant at the API Gateway layer to reduce backlog amplification
Asked VectorSync to pause the partner webhook provider and roll back the partner's retry configuration (VectorSync confirmed action at 19:15 UTC)
Shifted some serving traffic away from affected nodes using a soft-weighted route change to reduce pressure on nodes experiencing NVML resets
resolution: Partial mitigation succeeded: ingress rate-limits + partner pause brought 5xx floor down and stopped further NVML resets by 19:23 UTC. Full remediation requires follow-up work: hardening accept-queue backpressure, aggressive connection culling for large payloads, and runtime kernel allocation limits. Owner: runtime team. Targeted follow-up ticket created to harden prefetch and batching heuristics.
next_steps: (runtime) Create a follow-up ticket to add a hard cap on batch allocation size when accept-queue exceeds threshold
(api-gateway) Implement per-tenant connection-culling policy for long-lived HTTP/2 streams to prevent backlog amplification
(platform) Add automated mitigation playbook for partner-driven webhook storms (runbook link created)
Schedule postmortem with VectorSync and partner to share findings and confirm configuration changes
